changelog.why: The draft job ordering_a_replacement_debit_card (reissue debit card after fraud closure) is this library job. Its steps r1-r6 are covered by get_cards/get_accounts, check_order, history, entry_wait, excess_fee_choice_step, ask_delivery/ask_design/confirm_addr, order and inform, which match the draft's rules from docs 023 and 029.

rules: Entry: standard shipping only, $0
Mid, Premium and Elite: no waiting period
Entry: 48-hour wait after card closure, which still applies after the excess fee
CLASSIC is $0 at every tier and is the default
No order while a card order is already pending
Elite: all delivery is free
Elite has unlimited replacements
Fees are charged when the card is ordered
Cards issued for other reasons do not count toward the limit
The limit runs over a rolling 12 months
delivery_fee and design_fee are the account tier's own figures, never the general list price

verdicts.clause: read each card's status, issue_reason and date_issued
verdicts.unsupported: Unlock; status, issue_reason and date_issued
verdicts.why: The quote supports calling get_debit_cards_by_account_id_7823 to look up a checking account's debit cards, but the visible field list stops at card_id and account_id, and nothing in this step's quote names status, issue_reason or date_issued or any need to unlock the tool.

verdicts.clause: ask the customer when it was closed
verdicts.why: The closure time of a card closed before this conversation is marked as no document's, and the step turns it into a question for the customer rather than a rule.

verdicts.clause: The closure time is the time recorded right after the card was closed in this conversation (note_closure_time in closing_cancelling_a_debit_card)
verdicts.unsupported: the time recorded right after the card was closed in this conversation (note_closure_time in closing_cancelling_a_debit_card)
verdicts.why: The quote counts the 48 hours from card closure, but no quote says the closure time comes from a note_closure_time record in another procedure.

verdicts.clause: Give the earliest time (closure time plus 48 hours, compared with get_time) ... and do not order now
verdicts.why: derived: the quote '48-hour waiting period after card closure before a replacement can be ordered' fixes the earliest order time as closure plus 48 hours, so ordering before then is barred.

verdicts.clause: only STANDARD delivery is available ($0, 7-10 business days)
verdicts.unsupported: 7-10 business days
verdicts.why: The quote supports standard shipping only at a $0 delivery_fee for Entry, but it gives no delivery time.

verdicts.clause: $15 from checking, 3-5 business days. Use EXPEDITED (fee 15) only if the customer accepts; otherwise STANDARD (fee 0)
verdicts.unsupported: from checking, 3-5 business days; only if the customer accepts
verdicts.why: The quote supports Mid-tier expedited at $15 and standard at $0, but this step's quote does not say the fee is taken from checking, gives no 3-5 day delivery time, and does not make acceptance a condition.

verdicts.clause: Use a paid option only after the customer accepts the fee
verdicts.unsupported: only after the customer accepts
verdicts.why: The quote requires informing the customer before the order that the fee will be deducted from checking; it does not make the customer's acceptance a condition for placing the order.

verdicts.clause: use the fastest $0 delivery: Elite RUSH, Premium EXPEDITED, Mid ... STANDARD
verdicts.why: derived: doc 023's delivery list (STANDARD 7-10, EXPEDITED 3-5, RUSH 1-2 business days) ranks the speeds, and doc 029's quotes give Elite $0 for RUSH, Premium $0 for STANDARD and EXPEDITED, and Mid $0 only for STANDARD.

verdicts.clause: Entry STANDARD
verdicts.unsupported: Entry
verdicts.why: No quote in this step gives Entry delivery fees; the Mid quote is carried to Entry, and doc 023's general fees 'may vary based on account tier'.

verdicts.clause: For Premium and Elite, ask the customer which free design they want
verdicts.why: Which free design is best is marked as no document's, and the step makes it a question for the customer.

verdicts.clause: otherwise use CLASSIC
verdicts.unsupported: otherwise use CLASSIC
verdicts.why: The fee table supports giving the requested design only when its tier fee is $0, but when other designs are also $0 (e.g. Premium tier with CUSTOM at $15, where both CLASSIC and PREMIUM are $0), nothing in the quotes says to pick CLASSIC.

ensure_verified.why: Doc 023 requires verification and the policy says to verify only once per conversation.

get_accounts.why: Doc 009 names this tool for retrieving a customer's checking and savings accounts and lists the fields read.

per_account.why: Doc 023 has the agent confirm the linked checking account, and doc 029 sets policy by that account's tier, so each account is handled with its own tier.

clauses.clause: run the steps once per account, each with its own tier, and ask delivery and design separately for each
clauses.source: (1) Doc 029: replacement policies 'vary based on the customer's checking account tier'. (2) Doc 023 steps 2-5: each order is linked to one checking account, and delivery and design are asked for that order. (3) So each account's order uses that account's tier and its own delivery and design questions.

get_cards.why: Doc 028 names this tool for checking existing active or pending cards before ordering.

get_user.why: Doc 023 requires checking age by date_of_birth and a US address on file, which this tool returns.

get_time.why: Policy guideline 4 requires get_current_time whenever the current time is needed, and the 3-business-day, 12-month and 48-hour checks need it.

check_order.why: Each check is one of doc 023's eligibility requirements, and the active-card check follows from requirement 5 together with the order tool's error.

clauses.clause: there is no other ACTIVE card
clauses.source: (1) Doc 023 req 5: no more than 1 active debit card per checking account. (2) order_debit_card_5739 description: it errors with 'already has an active debit card. Maximum 1 active card per checking account.' (3) So an existing ACTIVE card on the account blocks the order.

clauses.clause: If a check fails, explain what blocks the order and stop
clauses.source: (1) Doc 023 lists these as eligibility requirements for ordering. (2) Doc 023 step 3 checks them before step 7 orders. (3) A failed requirement therefore means no order.

old_card_not_closed.why: A blocked closure leaves the card in a status that blocks or is not shown to allow a new order, and withholding the order where no passage decides is kept.

clauses.clause: do not order while the old card's closure was blocked
clauses.source: (1) Doc 025 req 3: only ACTIVE or PENDING cards can be closed. (2) So a card whose closure failed for another reason is still ACTIVE or PENDING. (3) Doc 023 reqs 5 and 8 and the order tool's active-card error block an order while such a card exists.

clauses.clause: do not order (card blocked for another reason, e.g. FROZEN)
clauses.source: Doc 025 and doc 023 do not say whether a FROZEN or otherwise unclosable card blocks a new order. The prohibition stays.

clauses.clause: a new card can be ordered once the old card is closed
clauses.source: Doc 025 closing step 6: 'If they need a new card, they can order one through the standard ordering process.'

tier.why: Doc 029 keys replacement rules to the checking account tier, doc 005 is the only passage assigning checking products to those tiers, and refusing to guess an unlisted product's fees is kept.

clauses.clause: Light Blue, Light Green and Green Fee-Free are ENTRY; Blue and Green are MID; Evergreen is PREMIUM; Bluest is ELITE
clauses.source: (1) Doc 029: policies vary by 'the customer's checking account tier' (ENTRY/MID/PREMIUM/ELITE) but lists no products. (2) Doc 005 assigns checking products to exactly these tiers. (3) So the account's product gives its tier.

clauses.clause: unlisted product: do not guess a tier, order nothing
clauses.source: Doc 029 requires 'the exact delivery_fee and design_fee amounts based on the tier rules', and doc 005 lists no tier for other products. No passage decides, so withholding the order stays.

clauses.clause: offer a transfer
clauses.source: Policy guideline 5: if the issue cannot be resolved, ask whether the user would like to be transferred.

history.why: Doc 029 gives the counting method, the per-tier maxima and the at-limit options.

clauses.clause: At the limit (count equals the tier maximum) the wait-or-fee options apply
clauses.source: (1) Doc 029: 'Maximum 2 [3, 5] replacement cards per rolling 12-month period'. (2) With the maximum already counted, a further replacement would exceed it. (3) So doc 029's 'exceeded the ... limit' options apply to that order.

excess_fee_choice_step.why: Doc 029 states the wait-or-pay choice for Entry ($25) and Mid ($15) and the fee notice before ordering.

clauses.clause: give the date the oldest counted card ages out
clauses.source: (1) Doc 029: 'wait until oldest replacement ages out of the 12-month window'. (2) Doc 029: the window is 'rolling 12-month'. (3) So the date is that card's date_issued plus 12 months.

wait_date.why: The age-out date follows from the rolling 12-month window, and for Entry the 48-hour closure wait also applies, so the later date governs.

clauses.clause: age-out date is the oldest counted card's date_issued plus 12 months
clauses.source: (1) Doc 029 counts cards by date_issued within a rolling 12-month period. (2) So the oldest counted card leaves the window 12 months after its date_issued.

clauses.clause: For Entry, use the later of that date and closure time plus 48 hours
clauses.source: (1) Doc 029 ENTRY lists the 48-hour wait after closure as a separate bullet from the limit. (2) Both must be met before ordering. (3) So the earliest order time is the later of the two.

entry_wait.why: Doc 029 states the Entry 48-hour wait and standard-only shipping, and asking for a closure time that no record holds is a question.

clauses.clause: closure time is the time recorded right after the card was closed in this conversation
clauses.source: (1) Policy guideline 4: the current time comes from get_current_time. (2) A closure made in this conversation therefore has its time read when it happens.

clauses.clause: if the card was closed before this conversation, ask the customer when it was closed
clauses.source: (1) Doc 028 lists the card fields, and none of them is a closure date. (2) No record holds the time. (3) So the step asks the customer for that fact.

entry_expedited_request.why: Doc 029 states Entry has standard shipping only at $0.

clauses.clause: 7-10 business days
clauses.source: Doc 023: 'STANDARD: Free shipping, arrives in 7-10 business days'.

excess_fee_then_wait.why: The Entry 48-hour wait is separate from the excess-fee option, and doc 029 says fees are charged when the card is ordered.

clauses.clause: the 48-hour wait still applies after the fee is accepted; do not order now
clauses.source: Doc 029 ENTRY offers the $25 fee only as the alternative to waiting out the 12-month window, and nothing lifts the 48-hour bullet. The prohibition stays.

clauses.clause: the fee will be charged when they order then
clauses.source: Doc 029: fees 'are AUTOMATICALLY CHARGED to the linked checking account when the card is ordered'.

ask_delivery.why: Each tier's delivery fees are stated in doc 029 and the times in doc 023, and omitting RUSH for Mid holds back an offer no passage naming Mid makes.

clauses.clause: Mid: STANDARD $0, EXPEDITED $15 (no RUSH offered)
clauses.source: Doc 029 MID lists only 'Standard ... or expedited shipping available'. Doc 023 lists RUSH generally with 'fees may vary based on account tier' but does not name Mid. The withheld offer stays.

mid_expedited_with_fee.why: Doc 029 gives the Mid expedited fee and doc 023 gives the times, and the customer's acceptance of the fee is a choice no record decides.

clauses.clause: otherwise STANDARD (fee 0)
clauses.source: Doc 029 MID: STANDARD is the only other delivery option, at delivery_fee $0.

elite_priority.why: Doc 029 states same-day shipping for Elite orders before 2pm EST.

fastest_paid_option.why: Each tier's quickest available option and its fee is stated in doc 029, with times from doc 023.

clauses.clause: Mid EXPEDITED $15 as quickest
clauses.source: Doc 029 MID names only standard and expedited. Doc 023's general RUSH listing does not name Mid. Withholding RUSH stays.

clauses.clause: Use a paid option only after the customer accepts the fee
clauses.source: Doc 029: 'Always inform the customer that the fee will be deducted ... before placing the order.'

offer_options.why: The $0 options per tier are stated in doc 029, speed comes from doc 023, and the choice among equally free designs is asked.

clauses.clause: use the fastest $0 delivery
clauses.source: (1) Doc 029 gives which delivery options are $0 per tier. (2) Doc 023 gives their times (RUSH 1-2, EXPEDITED 3-5, STANDARD 7-10). (3) Among free options, the fastest is the best.

clauses.clause: Both fees are 0
clauses.source: The chosen delivery and design are the doc 029 options listed at $0 for the tier.

best_free_no_fancy_design.why: CLASSIC is $0 at every tier, and the fastest $0 delivery per tier follows from doc 029 and doc 023.

clauses.clause: fastest $0 delivery
clauses.source: Doc 029 gives the $0 options per tier, and doc 023 gives their delivery times.

most_premium_free_both.why: Doc 029 gives the free shipping and design options per tier, and the Elite choice between two $0 designs is asked.

clauses.clause: design is PREMIUM for Premium tier
clauses.source: (1) Doc 029 PREMIUM TIER: CLASSIC $0 and PREMIUM design $0, CUSTOM $15. (2) PREMIUM (metallic silver) is the non-default design among the free ones.

clauses.clause: shipping is the fastest $0 option
clauses.source: Doc 029 gives the $0 options per tier, and doc 023 gives their times.

fastest_free_option.why: The $0 options and times are stated in doc 029 and doc 023, and CLASSIC is the default.

clauses.clause: Elite RUSH; Premium EXPEDITED; Mid and Entry STANDARD
clauses.source: Doc 029 gives the $0 delivery per tier, and doc 023 gives the times: RUSH 1-2, EXPEDITED 3-5, STANDARD 7-10.

ask_design.why: Doc 023 step 5 asks for the design, and doc 029 states each tier's design fees.

design_if_free.why: Doc 029 gives which designs are $0 per tier, and doc 023 makes CLASSIC the no-fee default.

clauses.clause: otherwise use CLASSIC
clauses.source: (1) Doc 023: 'CLASSIC: ... (default, no fee)'. (2) Doc 029: CLASSIC design_fee $0 at every tier. (3) CLASSIC is therefore the free design whenever the requested one is not $0.

confirm_addr.why: Doc 023 has the agent confirm the mailing address and notes insufficient funds fail the order, and doc 029 requires the deduction notice.

clauses.clause: US mailing address
clauses.source: Doc 023 req 9: 'valid US domestic address (international shipping is not available)'.

order.why: Doc 023 names the order tool, doc 029 requires exact tier fees, and the excess fee is the tool's optional parameter, used only when it applies.

clauses.clause: Pass excess_replacement_fee only if the customer accepted it (Entry 25, Mid 15)
clauses.source: (1) order_debit_card_5739 description: excess_replacement_fee is optional, 'if applicable'. (2) Doc 029: the $25 (Entry) or $15 (Mid) fee is the alternative to waiting once the limit is exceeded.

clauses.clause: no tier wait is pending
clauses.source: Doc 029 ENTRY: '48-hour waiting period after card closure before a replacement can be ordered'. The limit wait applies when the customer chose to wait or the tier is Premium.

inform.why: Doc 023 step 8 and its notes state the timeframe, the fees and app tracking.

order_error.why: Policy guideline 5 has the agent ask before transferring, and doc 042 names technical_system_error and the highest-tier rule.

clauses.clause: tell the customer what must be resolved
clauses.source: The order tool's error replies name the failing condition, for example insufficient funds, a minimum balance, or an existing active card.

R2.why: Doc 029 states 'No waiting period' for the MID, PREMIUM and ELITE tiers.

R3.why: Doc 029 states the 48-hour wait, and the excess fee is offered only against the 12-month limit, so the wait stands (kept).

R4.why: Doc 029 lists CLASSIC at $0 for every tier, and doc 023 calls it the default with no fee.

R10.why: Doc 029 states a rolling 12-month period for each limited tier.

R11.why: Doc 029 requires exact fees 'based on the tier rules below', and doc 023 says its list fees vary by account tier.

ensure_verified.why: Doc 023 requirement 1 and the policy's verification and no-reverification rules state both branches.

get_accounts.why: Doc 009 names the tool and the fields it returns.

per_account.why: Doc 023 step 2 states confirming the linked account, and doc 029 ties the policy to that account's tier, so each account's order is run on its own.

clauses.clause: run the steps once per account, each with its own tier, and ask delivery and design separately for each
clauses.source: (1) Doc 029: replacement policies 'vary based on the customer's checking account tier'. (2) Doc 023 steps 2-7 order one card linked to one confirmed checking account, asking delivery (step 4) and design (step 5) for that order. (3) So each account's order is a separate pass with its own tier and its own choices.

get_cards.why: Doc 028 names the tool and the fields status, issue_reason and date_issued.

get_user.why: Doc 023 requirements 7 and 9 need date_of_birth and the address on file, which the tool returns.

get_time.why: Policy guideline 4 requires get_current_time, and doc 023 (3 business days) and doc 029 (rolling 12 months, 48 hours) need the current time.

check_order.why: Each check is a doc 023 eligibility requirement, and stopping on a failure follows from them being requirements.

clauses.clause: there is no other ACTIVE card
clauses.source: (1) Doc 023 req 5: 'cannot have more than 1 active debit cards per checking account'. (2) Doc 028 use case 1: 'Before ordering a new debit card: Check if customer already has an active or pending card for the account'. (3) The order_debit_card_5739 description returns 'already has an active debit card. Maximum 1 active card per checking account.' (4) So an existing ACTIVE card blocks the order.

clauses.clause: If a check fails, explain what blocks the order and stop
clauses.source: (1) Doc 023 lists these as 'Eligibility requirements'. (2) Its step 3 checks them before step 7 orders. (3) A failed requirement therefore means no order.

old_card_not_closed.why: An unclosed ACTIVE or PENDING old card blocks the order under doc 023/028 and the tool description, and no passage permits ordering for any other unclosed card, so the prohibition stays.

clauses.clause: If the old card's closure was blocked, do not order
clauses.source: If the card stays ACTIVE, doc 023 req 5 and the order tool's active-card error block the order. If it stays PENDING, doc 023 req 8 blocks it. For a FROZEN card (doc 025 req 3 bars its closure), neither doc 023 nor doc 029 names the case either way, so the clause forbidding the write stays.

tier.why: Doc 005 is the only passage mapping products to the tier names doc 029 uses, and holding back an order for an unmapped product is a kept prohibition.

clauses.clause: Light Blue, Light Green, Green Fee-Free ENTRY; Blue, Green MID; Evergreen PREMIUM; Bluest ELITE
clauses.source: (1) Doc 029 sets replacement rules by 'the customer's checking account tier' (ENTRY/MID/PREMIUM/ELITE) but names no products. (2) Doc 005 names the checking products in each of those same tiers. (3) The account's product therefore gives its doc 029 tier.

clauses.clause: unlisted product: order nothing and offer a transfer
clauses.source: Doc 029 requires 'the exact delivery_fee and design_fee amounts based on the tier rules', and doc 005 lists no tier for other products. No passage decides the case, so holding back the order stays. Policy guideline 5 gives the transfer offer.

history.why: Doc 029 states the counting method and each tier's limit and remedy.

clauses.clause: At the limit (count equal to the tier maximum) the remedy applies
clauses.source: (1) Doc 029: 'Maximum 2 [3, 5] replacement cards per rolling 12-month period'. (2) The card being ordered is itself a replacement. (3) With the count already at the maximum, this order would exceed it, which triggers doc 029's 'If customer has exceeded the ... limit' remedy.

excess_fee_choice_step.why: Doc 029 states the wait-or-pay choice for Entry and Mid and the fee notice before ordering.

clauses.clause: give the date the oldest counted card ages out
clauses.source: (1) Doc 029: 'wait until oldest replacement ages out of the 12-month window'. (2) Doc 029 counts by date_issued over a 'rolling 12-month period'. (3) So the date is the oldest counted date_issued plus 12 months.

wait_date.why: The age-out date follows from doc 029's rolling window, and for Entry both of doc 029's conditions must hold, so the later date governs.

clauses.clause: age-out date is oldest counted date_issued plus 12 months
clauses.source: (1) Doc 029 counts 'cards issued within the last 12 months' by date_issued. (2) Doc 029 says 'wait until oldest replacement ages out'. (3) That card leaves the window 12 months after its date_issued.

clauses.clause: For Entry, the later of that date and closure plus 48 hours
clauses.source: (1) Doc 029 ENTRY lists the 48-hour wait after closure and the limit as separate rules. (2) An order must satisfy both. (3) So it is possible only at the later of the two dates.

entry_wait.why: Doc 029 states the 48-hour wait and Entry's standard-only shipping, and since no card field holds a closure time (doc 028), asking the customer is a question.

clauses.clause: earliest time is closure time plus 48 hours, compared with get_time
clauses.source: (1) Doc 029: '48-hour waiting period after card closure before a replacement can be ordered'. (2) Policy guideline 4 requires get_current_time for the current time. (3) The earliest order time is closure time plus 48 hours.

entry_expedited_request.why: Doc 029 ENTRY says standard shipping only, no expedited, delivery_fee $0, and doc 023 gives 7-10 business days.

excess_fee_then_wait.why: Paying the excess fee replaces only the limit wait, the separate 48-hour rule still holds, and fees are charged when the card is ordered.

clauses.clause: do not order now despite the accepted fee
clauses.source: (1) Doc 029 ENTRY: the $25 fee is the alternative only to waiting until 'oldest replacement ages out'. (2) The 48-hour wait after closure is a separate ENTRY rule. (3) So the fee does not lift the 48-hour wait.

clauses.clause: the fee will be charged when they order then
clauses.source: Doc 029: 'All applicable fees (shipping, design, excess replacement) are AUTOMATICALLY CHARGED ... when the card is ordered.'

ask_delivery.why: Doc 029 states each tier's delivery fees and doc 023 the delivery times, and not offering RUSH to Mid is a kept hold-back.

clauses.clause: Mid: STANDARD $0, EXPEDITED $15 (no RUSH offered)
clauses.source: Doc 029 MID names only standard and expedited. Doc 023 lists RUSH $35 generally ('fees may vary based on account tier') without naming Mid. No passage naming Mid decides RUSH, so the offer stays held back.

mid_expedited_with_fee.why: Doc 029 states Mid's $15 expedited fee and doc 023 its 3-5 days, and using it turns on the customer's choice, which no record holds.

clauses.clause: EXPEDITED only if the customer accepts; otherwise STANDARD
clauses.source: (1) Doc 023 step 4 asks the customer's preferred delivery option and explains fees. (2) Doc 029 MID offers only STANDARD $0 or EXPEDITED $15. (3) If the customer declines the fee, STANDARD is the remaining option.

elite_priority.why: Doc 029 ELITE states same-business-day shipping before 2pm EST.

fastest_paid_option.why: Doc 029 fees and doc 023 speeds give the quickest option per tier, and the paid choice is the customer's.

clauses.clause: quickest per tier: Premium RUSH, Elite RUSH, Mid EXPEDITED, Entry STANDARD
clauses.source: (1) Doc 023 times: RUSH 1-2, EXPEDITED 3-5, STANDARD 7-10 business days. (2) Doc 029 options per tier: Premium and Elite have RUSH, Mid has up to EXPEDITED, Entry has STANDARD only. (3) Taking the fastest available option in each tier gives this list.

clauses.clause: Mid limited to EXPEDITED
clauses.source: Doc 029 MID names no RUSH, and doc 023's general RUSH entry does not name Mid, so the hold-back stays.

offer_options.why: Doc 029 states the $0 options per tier, doc 023 ranks speeds, and no passage ranks equally free designs, so asking is a question.

clauses.clause: fastest $0 delivery: Elite RUSH, Premium EXPEDITED, Mid and Entry STANDARD
clauses.source: (1) Doc 029 $0 delivery: Elite all three, Premium STANDARD and EXPEDITED, Mid and Entry STANDARD. (2) Doc 023 speed order: RUSH, then EXPEDITED, then STANDARD. (3) The fastest $0 option per tier follows.

best_free_no_fancy_design.why: Fastest $0 delivery is derived as in offer_options, and CLASSIC is $0 at every tier (doc 029) and the default (doc 023).

clauses.clause: fastest $0 delivery per tier
clauses.source: (1) Doc 029 gives the $0 delivery options per tier. (2) Doc 023 gives the speed order RUSH, EXPEDITED, STANDARD. (3) The fastest $0 option per tier follows.

most_premium_free_both.why: Doc 029 gives the $0 options and doc 023 the speeds, PREMIUM is $0 only for Premium and Elite, and the Elite choice between PREMIUM and CUSTOM is asked.

clauses.clause: most premium free shipping is the fastest $0 option
clauses.source: (1) Doc 023 orders STANDARD, EXPEDITED, RUSH by speed and fee. (2) Doc 029 gives the $0 options per tier. (3) The top $0 option per tier is Elite RUSH, Premium EXPEDITED, Mid and Entry STANDARD.

clauses.clause: design PREMIUM for Premium tier, CLASSIC for Mid and Entry
clauses.source: (1) Doc 029: Premium tier PREMIUM design $0 but CUSTOM $15. (2) Doc 029: Entry and Mid have only CLASSIC at $0. (3) So the top $0 design is PREMIUM for Premium tier and CLASSIC for Mid and Entry.

fastest_free_option.why: Doc 029 $0 options and doc 023 speeds give the fastest free delivery, and CLASSIC is the stated default.

clauses.clause: Elite RUSH, Premium EXPEDITED, Mid and Entry STANDARD
clauses.source: (1) Doc 029 gives the $0 delivery options per tier. (2) Doc 023 gives the times 1-2, 3-5 and 7-10 business days. (3) The fastest $0 option per tier follows.

ask_design.why: Doc 023 step 5 and doc 029's design fees by tier state every figure.

design_if_free.why: The customer sets the condition, doc 029 gives the tier fee, and CLASSIC is $0 at every tier and the default.

clauses.clause: otherwise use CLASSIC
clauses.source: (1) The customer wants the design only if it is free. (2) Doc 029: CLASSIC design_fee $0 at every tier. (3) Doc 023: CLASSIC is the 'default, no fee'.

confirm_addr.why: Doc 023 step 6, the doc 023 insufficient-funds note and the doc 029 fee notice state each clause, and a US address follows from doc 023 req 9.

clauses.clause: the mailing address must be in the US
clauses.source: Doc 023 req 9: 'valid US domestic address (international shipping is not available)'.

order.why: Doc 023 step 7 and doc 029 give the call and its exact tier fees, and the tool description makes excess_replacement_fee optional, applying only when doc 029's limit is exceeded and the fee is chosen.

clauses.clause: excess_replacement_fee: Entry 25, Mid 15; omit when none applies
clauses.source: (1) The order_debit_card_5739 description: 'excess_replacement_fee (number, optional): Fee for exceeding replacement limit, if applicable'. (2) Doc 029 sets $25 for Entry and $15 for Mid when the limit is exceeded and the customer pays rather than waits.

clauses.clause: no ACTIVE card on the account
clauses.source: (1) Doc 023 req 5. (2) Doc 028 use case 1. (3) The tool's error 'already has an active debit card'.

inform.why: Doc 023 step 8 and its tracking note state it.

order_error.why: The tool replies give the failure, policy guideline 5 requires asking before a transfer, and doc 042 says to choose the highest-tier code that applies, with technical_system_error for system errors.
